sections.html:
Hialeah was incorporated in 1925 and marked its centennial in 2025. It lies in Miami-Dade County, so the Miami-Dade Tax Collector sends your bill and the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser sets your value and handles exemptions. Hialeah Park, a National Register site opened the same year as the city, remains the best-known landmark inside city limits.

Because the county, not the city, controls most of what a seller deals with, this page walks through the county offices, the dates that matter, and the paperwork a buyer will ask for.

sections.h2: Miami-Dade tax bills and due dates
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade County Tax Collector mails annual notices at the end of October, and online payment opens the same day. The office is at 200 NW 2nd Avenue, Miami, and the phone number is 305-375-5448. BillExpress subscribers get the notice by email on the mailing date.

The collector does not set the tax. Value comes from the Property Appraiser, less exemptions, and each taxing authority sets its own rate. If the 2026 real estate taxes are not paid before June 1, 2027, a tax certificate may be issued, and the annual certificate sale starts June 1, 2027.

  • Water, road and sewer assessments, such as OJUS, are collected in annual installments. A bill containing one must be paid by May 31 or a certificate is sold for the remaining lien balance.
  • Discounts for paying early step down each month, with the largest in November.

sections.h2: What Amendment 3 changes for a Hialeah homestead
sections.html:
Voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, and it takes effect January 1, 2027. The change applies to non-school property taxes, and the school board exemption stays at $25,000.

Homestead exemption amounts, Miami-Dade
Tax yearUp to, non-school taxes
Through 2026$50,000 (state homestead exemption)
2027$150,000 for residents established by December 31, 2026
2028$250,000 for the same group
2029 onwardAdjusted yearly for positive CPI change

People who establish Florida residency after December 31, 2026 start at up to $50,000 and generally reach the larger amount in the fifth year of receiving a homestead exemption. That provision depends on federal constitutional limits and implementing legislation, so a buyer moving from another state should ask the appraiser how the rules apply.

sections.h2: How to file for, keep or lose homestead
sections.html:
• Deadline: applications and documents are due March 1. Late applications may be accepted until the date on the TRIM notice, with a possible $15 fee and a Value Adjustment Board petition.
  • Residency proof: one item is enough, such as a Florida driver license, vehicle registration, voter registration, a W-2 or tax return, bank statements, utility payments or a recorded Declaration of Domicile.
  • Where: the online Application Portal, or in person at the Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1 Street, Suite 710, or the South Dade Government Center. Phone 305-375-4712.
  • Renewal: homestead owners get a renewal receipt in late December, and a property with a deed change gets none.

Renting the house puts the exemption at risk. If a change in status goes unreported, back taxes can reach ten years of exempted taxes, plus 15 percent interest per year and a penalty of 50 percent of the taxes exempted. Report any change before you list the house for rent or sale.

sections.h2: Deed tax for a Hialeah seller
sections.html:
Miami-Dade is the one county with its own rate. The deed tax there is 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cent surtax per $100 that does not apply to a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. Every other county uses 70 cents.

The clerk collects the tax at recording, and everyone named on the deed is liable no matter what the contract says. Quit claim deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure are taxable, while a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not. Check the Miami-Dade Clerk's current schedule for the recording charges that will appear on your closing statement.

Ask the City of Hialeah building department for the permit history of your address, and pull any open or expired permit before you list. Roofs, window replacements, electrical panels, additions and fences are what buyers ask about most.

Unpermitted work gives a buyer three choices: have it permitted, have it repaired, or price it in. A cash buyer may accept the house with open items, but a lender-financed buyer usually will not. Get the facts first, then choose the route.

sections.h2: What if you disagree with an assessment or an exemption denial?
sections.html:
A value challenge is a petition filed with the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes. A denied exemption can go to the value adjustment board 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. The Miami-Dade appraiser mails the proposed notice by the end of August, and the late-filing date printed on it is usually 25 days after mailing.

A sale is a good moment to check the parcel record. Confirm the owner name, the exemptions listed and the mailing address on the tax roll, so the notice reaches you.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Hialeah house
sections.html:
• Listing with an agent: wider exposure, more showings and inspection requests, and a closing that depends on the buyer's financing.
  • Selling to a cash buyer: a purchase in present condition, with timing you can agree on, and a price you should compare against a listing estimate.
  • Selling to a relative: still a taxable deed event, and it changes the property's assessment if the cap resets.

With any buyer, ask for written terms, the date money reaches you, and who pays recording and deed tax. Keep the Miami-Dade tax bill, any assessment notice and permit records with the contract.

An owner who applies for homestead in another Florida county must cancel the Miami-Dade exemption. Applications can be tracked through a status page, and suspected homestead fraud goes to an investigation unit at 305-375-3402. After buying a house with a deed change, a new owner files a fresh application, because no renewal receipt arrives for that property.

faqs.a: Miami-Dade County, so the Miami-Dade Tax Collector and Property Appraiser handle your tax bill and exemptions.

faqs.q: What is the Miami-Dade deed tax rate?
faqs.a: 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cent surtax per $100. The surtax does not apply to a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: When is the homestead deadline in Miami-Dade?
faqs.a: March 1. A late application may still be taken until the date shown on the TRIM notice, and a $15 fee may apply.

faqs.q: What happens if I rent out a homestead house?
faqs.a: The exemption can be lost, and unreported changes can be back taxed for ten years with 15 percent interest and a 50 percent penalty.

faqs.q: When does a tax certificate sale happen?
faqs.a: The annual sale starts June 1, 2027 for unpaid 2026 real estate taxes.
